corrections.original_claim: The live gallery is salons.gallery_urls plus salon_portfolio_images, 'both written by ONE route: app/api/salons/[slug]/gallery/route.ts'.
corrections.truth: There are THREE writers to salons.gallery_urls, and only one of them dual-writes salon_portfolio_images. The onboarding wizard is a completely separate, client-side write path the recon never found.
corrections.evidence: (a) app/[locale]/onboarding/salon/page.tsx:322-324 mounts <ImageUpload bucket="salon-gallery" pathPrefix="onboarding"> which uploads DIRECT to the bucket from the browser (components-legacy/ui/ImageUpload.tsx:116-118 `supabase.storage.from(bucket).upload(fileName,...)`, no API route), collects URLs into photoUrls (:375, :687 onUpload={setPhotoUrls}), then POSTs them at :494 `fetch("/api/salons")` with `gallery_urls: photoUrls` (:516). (b) app/api/salons/route.ts:656 destructures gallery_urls and :707 writes `gallery_urls: gallery_urls?.filter(Boolean) || []` , grep for salon_portfolio_images in that file: zero hits, so no portfolio row is created. corrections.original_claim: A salon owner CAN delete their own gallery photo today. Full path works (button -> route -> storage -> both tables).
corrections.truth: It works only for photos uploaded THROUGH the dashboard GalleryManager. For onboarding-uploaded photos it fails twice over, and the second failure is a textbook silent no-op that returns 200 {success:true}. (1) The dashboard grid renders exclusively from salon_portfolio_images, so a photo with no portfolio row is INVISIBLE in the dashboard and has no delete button at all. The migration's backfill is a one-shot INSERT, so every salon onboarded after 2026-07-25 has gallery_urls entries with no portfolio row. (2) Even when the row exists (pre-migration backfilled onboarding photos), the DELETE handler's storage-path guard refuses to remove the bytes, because onboarding objects live at `onboarding/<file>`, not `<salonId>/<file>`. The route logs a warn, deletes the DB row, and still returns success. The photo disappears from the site while the object stays world-readable in the public salon-gallery bucket forever.
corrections.evidence: Guard: app/api/salons/[slug]/gallery/route.ts:264-266 `segs.length === 2 && segs[0] === slug` , for an onboarding URL segs[0] is the literal string "onboarding", so isOwnSalonPath is false, :275-277 logs `Refused cross-salon storage delete` and skips the remove, then :284-289 still filters gallery_urls and :309 returns `{ success: true }`. Path shape written by onboarding: components-legacy/ui/ImageUpload.tsx:113-114 `const prefix = pathPrefix ? "${pathPrefix}/" : ""; const fileName = "${prefix}${Date.now()}-..."`. Dashboard render source: components-legacy/dashboard/GalleryManager.tsx:35 `useState<GalleryPhoto[]>` <- :54 `fetch('/api/salons/${salonId}/gallery')` -> route.ts:31 `.from("salon_portfolio_images")`; :252 `photos.map(...)` is the only grid source. One-shot backfill: supabase/migrations/20260725120000_salon_portfolio_images.sql:73-82 (a plain `insert ... select` in the migration body, not a trigger).

net_picture:
Sixteen of the twenty-two claims survive verification intact and the recon's central architecture read is correct: salon_photos is a dead orphan (0 rows, INTEGER salon_id against a UUID salons.id, zero code call sites), the live gallery is salons.gallery_urls plus the newer salon_portfolio_images mirror, no admin can delete any salon photo (app/api/salons/[slug]/gallery/route.ts:237 is owner-only with no admin branch, and nothing under app/api/admin/** touches gallery_urls, salon_portfolio_images or the salon-gallery bucket except the seeder at seed-test-salons/route.ts:185), there is no 'photo' report target (078_content_reports.sql:4 CHECK is salon|review|user), there is no per-salon reviews toggle anywhere (zero grep hits, no column among the 104 on salons), the settings-save allowlist trap at app/api/salons/[slug]/route.ts:72-91 is real, and the review-photo upload does return 200 {success:true, photos:[]} on failure.

Three things are wrong, and the two biggest ones point the same direction: the recon only ever looked at the dashboard gallery path and missed the onboarding one.

First, gallery_urls is NOT written by one route. The onboarding wizard uploads straight from the browser into the salon-gallery bucket (onboarding/salon/page.tsx:322-324 -> ImageUpload.tsx:116-118, no API route) and persists the URLs through POST /api/salons (route.ts:707), which never inserts a salon_portfolio_images row. Second, and this is the finding that changes the build order: 'a salon owner CAN delete their own photo today, full path works' is only true for photos uploaded through the dashboard. Onboarding photos land at the storage path `onboarding/<file>` instead of `<salonId>/<file>`, so the DELETE handler's own path guard (:264-266, `segs[0] === slug`) refuses to remove the bytes, logs a warn at :275-277, deletes the DB entry anyway, and returns `{success:true}` at :309. The photo vanishes from the site while the object stays world-readable in a public bucket. Worse, because the migration's backfill is a one-shot INSERT (20260725120000_...sql:73-82) rather than a trigger, every salon onboarded after 2026-07-25 has gallery_urls entries with no portfolio row at all, and GalleryManager renders exclusively from salon_portfolio_images (:35 <- :54 <- route.ts:31, grid at :252), so those photos have no delete button in the dashboard whatsoever. That is a live silent no-op in exactly the area being extended, and it must be fixed before an admin-delete branch is bolted onto the same handler, or the admin delete inherits the identical byte-orphaning bug.

Third, the 'admin can mark a reported salon action_taken with no content action' hole is API-only, not UI-reachable: app/[locale]/dashboard/reports/page.tsx has no status dropdown, only Review (:265), Dismiss (:273) and a review-gated Hide (:280-282). The permissive surface is lib/validations.ts:844-848, which accepts any of the four statuses regardless of target_type.

Beyond that, several numbers are wrong without changing conclusions: the allowlist has 36 keys not 27 (and does include cover_photo_url, a photo key), salons has 104 columns not 99, the 'reviews' feature flag has nine check sites not four, the salon_photos grep misses lib/stock-image.ts:6, the review-photos migration grep misses a comment hit in 20260720155639_avatars_bucket.sql:7, and seven of the nine upload-path citations point at the handler declaration rather than the storage call. Two claims rest on evidence nobody re-derived this session and should be labelled as such: 'the review-photos bucket has no INSERT policy' is a 2026-07-16 third-party pg_policies reading (the fake-200 itself is first-hand), and the reviews_update_own_48h missing-WITH-CHECK escalation is a correct reading of the policy text plus an untested exploit inference. And salon_portfolio_images still does not appear in _inventory/_db-columns.json, _db-snapshot.json or SURFACE.json (all captured 2026-07-12, before the 2026-07-25 migration), with a hand-written type at lib/database.types.ts:6031, so step zero remains: prove the table exists live and refresh the snapshot before building anything on it.
